messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing nvme queue_depth spikes on gnode pools in us-west1 right after the inter-region mesh heartbeat at 02:03 UTC. GPU attach requests are timing out for ~10-30s windows.
kevin: logs? metrics? which hosts?
maria: us-west1-a/b clusters, ~12 nodes, avgqu-sz jumps from 0.2 -> 18. sample kernel log: ```Kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456```. Also iostat snapshot: ```Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 12.00 8.00 1500.00 800.00 80.00 14.5 25.2 2.10 99.6```
jia: This pattern matches previous metadata-sync heartbeats — when the region mesh heartbeat runs it temporarily stalls metadata updates which causes janitor/scrub tasks to queue IO. The scrub window plus heartbeat = IO storms.
oliver: Quick mitigation: throttle the janitor/scrub concurrency and add per-node IO rate limits. We can flip a feature flag to increase janitor backoff to 20m and set cleaner concurrency to 2.
kevin: Can we reproduce with fio before changing production? If we can trigger the exact timing we can be confident the backoff helps.
maria: ran a quick fio that simulates scrub pattern during heartbeat, reproduced avgqu-sz spikes. command used: ```fio --name=meta-scrub --rw=randread --bs=16k --ioengine=libaio --numjobs=4 --iodepth=32 --size=1G```. Result: large tail latency, device util spikes.
jia: Vendor counters show increased async completion latency on those NVMe controllers (we parsed SMART logs). I opened a vendor ticket, they suspect a microcode path that mis-handles bursty submission when controller is busy with admin/heartbeat work.
oliver: Interim ops plan: 1) flip janitor backoff flag in us-west regions (canary 3 nodes), 2) add node-level ionice/blkio throttling for nvme devices, 3) raise GPU attach timeout from 30s -> 60s in the scheduler to avoid immediate failures. I'll push the backoff patch now.
maria: Pushed backoff to canary nodes, monitoring dashboards show avgqu-sz down to ~3 on canary. GPU attach failures dropped to zero on canary.
kevin: Good. For long-term: vendor FW upgrade + we should avoid synchronized global heartbeats overlapping with scrub windows. Suggest randomizing heartbeat jitter and adding a small scrub jitter.
jia: Agree. I'll add jitter to heartbeat and add jitter to scrub cron in the scheduler config: ```scrub: { enabled: true, concurrency: 2, backoff_minutes: 20, cron_jitter_minutes: 5 }```
oliver: I'll file the fw upgrade rollout plan for low-traffic window and update runbook with rate-limit steps. Also adding monitoring alert for avgqu-sz > 10 for > 1m to auto-throttle scrub via feature flag.
maria: Also found 2 nodes with minor SMART reallocated sectors count rising — flagged them for disk replacement in the next maintenance window.
kevin: Thanks team. Who's owning the vendor escalation?
jia: I am owner, ticket #VEND-9123, shared logs and fio traces. Vendor asked for controller dump; will coordinate.
infra-bot: deploy: feature-flag janitor-backoff toggled on 3 canary nodes in us-west1 at 02:40 UTC by oliver
maria: Nice. Monitor looks stable for now. Will update thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
